subject: Staged SLA commitment: pilot -> production pricing corridors
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anna Morales <anna.morales@brightpeak.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staged SLA commitment: pilot -> production pricing corridors

Anna —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, attached is a compact proposal for a staged SLA commitment to support BrightPeak's pilot and then scale into production. High level:

- Pilot phase (3 months): light commit covering expected qps with a modest per-token uplift; limited credits for non-Beta incidents but guaranteed response windows for Sev1/Sev2.
- Transition corridor (months 4–6): phased discounts that kick in as committed throughput ramps; we lock in latency SLOs at each corridor.
- Production annualization: a single blended rate or laddered volume bands with an upfront commitment discount and optional 24x7 escalation retainer.

Key asks from us to make the numbers concrete: an estimate of peak tokens/day during pilot, expected growth rate each month, and whether you need 24x7 on-call for P1 or business-hours with an on-call fallback.

I attached a one-sheet (pilot_service_matrix.xlsx) and a short SLO/corridor summary (slo-corridor-summary.pdf). If you want, Laura can map the pricing corridor to specific commit bands and show the anchoring math.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm pilot sizing and any special blackout dates (holiday surge windows).
2) We send a Mutual Action Plan (MUP) and sample redlines (DocuSign-ready).
3) Laura and I will schedule a 30-min pricing walkthrough and finalize escalation roster requirements.

Appreciate it — talk soon.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. Quick clarifications so we can circulate internally: 

1) Escalation coverage: for pilot we expect standard North America business hours (Mon–Fri, 9–6 PT) with a named on-call engineer for P1 outside hours (on-call rotation at our cost is fine). If we move to production, we likely will need 24x7 coverage for P1 by the end of the first quarter.
2) Credits: can you confirm whether credit calculations are based on rolling 30-day uptime or per-month buckets? We have some compliance needs around SLA measurement windows.
3) Holiday surge: our busiest window is late November — if pilot overlaps any prep work for that (unlikely) we may want a one-time scale allowance.

Also, please call out any minimum term required to get the pilot pricing (e.g., do we need a 6‑month commit to access corridor discounts?).

Anna

Subject: Re: Staged SLA commitment: pilot -> production pricing corridors

Anna —

Thanks for the quick questions. I pulled the corridor math into the attached summary and a short example below to make it concrete.

Pilot assumptions (example):
- Expected pilot commit: 150M tokens/month (avg) with 1.5x peak buffer.
- Measurement window for credits: rolling 30-day window (this simplifies credit calculations for seasonal surges).

Pricing corridor (illustrative):
- Pilot rate (months 0–3): Base + 12% per-token uplift vs. production list. No annual term required — pilot can be month‑to‑month but requires a minimum 3-month notice to cancel early to ensure capacity planning.
- Transition corridor (months 4–6): If commit increases to >= 2x pilot baseline within the corridor, apply a 7% retroactive credit to pilot months and reduce per-token uplift to +6%.
- Production annualization: 12-month commit -> additional 10–18% discount depending on volume bands and whether 24x7 retainer is purchased.

Escalation & coverage notes: 
- Business-hours (default): Mon–Fri 9–6 PT, named SE on-call for P1 outside hours. P1 acknowledgment target within 30 minutes; resolution SLA depends on severity matrix.
- 24x7 option: +monthly retainer (example: $15k/mo) which guarantees 30-minute P1 acknowledgement and direct on-call escalation to the engineering on-call with a two-hour follow-through target.
- Failover / regional credits: if BrightPeak requires guaranteed regional failover in EU/ASIA, we add a regional availability premium to cover cross-region standby capacity (typically a +8–12% uplift).

Credits calculation example (rolling 30-day):
- If rolling availability < 99.5% -> 5% credit of monthly invoice.
- < 99.0% -> 10% credit plus incident RCA in 7 business days.
- < 98.0% -> 20% credit and escalation review.

Attachments: I included slo-corridor-summary.pdf and a draft MUP (mup-draft.docx) with milestones and signoff owners.

If this matches what you need, Jonas and I can prepare a one-page MUP and a clean DocuSign package with the production rate table and optional retainer add-on.

Best —
Laura Bennett
